time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 = t 0
pixel_convention: x to the right, y down, origin top-left of the image, full resolution
background: flat uniform grey (RGB ~132,126,135), no ground, horizon, markings or other static objects; no shadows

camera.motion: static (background is featureless and constant; object shapes/sizes constant; no shift detectable)
camera.perspective: pure side view, both objects move horizontally in the image plane; apparent sizes constant over the clip (airplane 800 x 239 px, car 121 x 41 px), so each object stays at constant depth. Pixel length ratio airplane/car = 800/121 = 6.6, close to a real A320 (~37 m) / Cybertruck (~5.7 m) ratio of ~6.5, so one common scale from the prior's object (2D convention) looks consistent.

objects.name: airplane
objects.description: white Air China passenger jet (A320-like), red phoenix logo on tail fin, side view, nose pointing right; upper half of frame
objects.visible_frames: 3-40 (partially: nose enters at left frames 3-17; fully visible 18-38; nose exits right edge from frame 39)
objects.reference_point: cx_est, cy_est = centre of full-object bounding box (for edge-cut frames reconstructed from the visible nose/tail edge with the full length 800 px)

full_view_extents_px.fuselage_vertical_extent: rows ~394-480 (about 86 px tall), fuselage centre line y ~437

objects.name: car

objects.reference_point: cx_centroid (smoothest, mask centroid) or cx_bbox; y constant (bbox centre 607, bottom of wheels 627)
